rationale: All 7 prior findings are resolved in the fix-up diff. CR-001: tools.py wraps handler.execute() in try/finally dispatching to client.dispose() (relational) or client.close() (InfluxDB). CR-002: InfluxDBDialectHandler.execute() wraps the query body in try/finally with client.close(). CR-003: RelationalDialectHandler.error_hint() uses nested try/finally — list_schema() in the inner try, engine.dispose() in the inner finally, with graceful fallback if schema fetch fails. CR-004: None-measurement guard (if measurement is None: continue) added before measurement is used as dict key or interpolated. CR-005: config.bucket and measurement escaped with .replace('"', '\"') in all Flux f-string literals. CR-006: list_tables_and_columns() now has if self.config is None: raise ValueError guard before _get_handler(). CR-007: Bare except Exception fallback added to healthcheck() after the SQLOperationalError clause, wrapping all other exceptions in ConnectionError. One minor observation: InfluxDB execute() now closes the client internally AND tools.py outer finally also calls client.close() — a redundant double-close. The InfluxDB Python client close() is idempotent; this is not a runtime error, data loss, or API issue and does not warrant a new finding. No new high-risk issues introduced by the fix-up diff.
